about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: the spec sheet (time: Google Calendar, deadlines from every pillar (homework due dates, bills from Midas), the shape of the day)
tasks.why: Kairos Meridian is a seat on the desk with no page yet. Joseph wants each pillar developed on its own; the first step is a spec Claude can build from.
steps: Write the spec for Kairos Meridian: time: Google Calendar, deadlines from every pillar (homework due dates, bills from Midas), the shape of the day.
At least 6 data sources with their real API names and documentation URLs (open each one); say plainly when something has no public API.
Four first screens, each listing every number on it and where it comes from.
Five 'done when' checks that can be tested on a phone.
Event titles stay in Joseph's calendar; the page reads them live.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with these 6 headings, in this order: 1 Purpose (one sentence) | 2 Data sources (a table: source | what it gives | how to get it (API name) | docs URL | sign-in type | cost | limits) | 3 First four screens (for each: its name, every number and list on it, where each comes from) | 4 Version 1 done when (5 checks Claude can test) | 5 Privacy (what never leaves the device) | 6 What Joseph must do once (accounts, keys, apps)

tasks.done_when: All 6 headings, at least 6 sources with working docs URLs, 4 screens, 5 testable checks.
checks: Claude checks each 'done when' can be tested without asking Joseph.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
an API that does not exist or a docs URL for something else
a screen that lists a number with no source

tasks.title: An ICS test file with 40 made-up events that cover every hard case
tasks.why: Kairos will import calendars; Claude needs a file that breaks weak parsers.
steps: Write one valid iCalendar file (RFC 5545) with 40 VEVENTs: 5 all-day, 3 multi-day, 6 weekly RRULE (with BYDAY), 4 monthly RRULE (BYMONTHDAY and BYSETPOS), 3 with EXDATE, 3 in America/Los_Angeles, 3 in Europe/London, 3 in Asia/Tokyo (with VTIMEZONE blocks), 2 across the 2026-03-08 and 2026-11-01 US clock changes, 4 overlapping, 2 crossing midnight, 2 with a 0-minute duration.
Put the case name in each SUMMARY (e.g. 'weekly MO,WE,FR until 2026-12-31').
tasks.done_when: One file that a strict parser (python icalendar) reads with no error, 40 events, every case present.
checks: Claude parses it and expands the rules for Nov 2026 - Mar 2027.

tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: the yearly deadlines a California homeowner and driver actually has
tasks.why: Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.
tasks.unlocks: Kairos puts each one on the calendar with its real rule, so property tax, registration and tax dates stop being remembered by hand.
steps: List every yearly deadline from these agencies that applies to someone who owns a home in Kern County, drives a registered car and a registered motorcycle, and files California and federal income tax: Kern County Treasurer-Tax Collector (both property-tax installments, supplemental bills), California DMV (vehicle and motorcycle registration, smog check rule for a 2025 hybrid, license renewal), Franchise Tax Board and IRS (filing, extension, the four estimated-tax dates), Covered California open enrollment, voter registration deadlines.
Open the agency's own page for each and copy the rule as written; compute next_due from today.
Leave out anything that does not apply to that person; say 'not stated' rather than guess.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below and nothing else

fields.name: title
fields.rule: what is due, under 60 characters, e.g. 'Property tax, first installment'

fields.name: rule
fields.rule: the date rule exactly as the agency states it, e.g. 'due Nov 1, delinquent after Dec 10 at 5 p.m.'

fields.name: next_due
fields.rule: the next date this falls on from today; if the rule moves for weekends, apply it

fields.name: repeats
fields.type: one of: yearly, every 2 years, twice a year, monthly
fields.rule: how often

fields.name: applies_if
fields.rule: who it applies to, e.g. 'owns a home in Kern County', 'has a registered vehicle'

fields.name: penalty
fields.rule: the penalty in the agency's words, or 'not stated'

fields.name: agency
fields.rule: the agency's name

fields.name: url
fields.rule: the exact page that shows this row, opened by you today; never a home page or search page

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: the sentence on that page that proves the row, copied word for word (under 300 characters)

fields.name: as_of
fields.rule: the date you read the page

example.title: Property tax, first installment
example.rule: Due November 1; delinquent after 5 p.m. December 10
example.applies_if: owns real property in Kern County
example.penalty: 10% penalty if not paid by the delinquency date

self_check: Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the maker's or agency's own site (not a blog, forum, wiki or AI summary).
Every quote is copied word for word from that page and is on it now.
No row is a copy of another with the names changed.
Numbers have their unit in the field name or the unit field, never inside the text.
The file is valid JSON (or the exact markdown headings asked for) and is named exactly as asked.
30 rows, or fewer with a line at the end of the file saying which agencies had nothing more.
tasks.done_when: 30 rows exactly in the shape, every self-check line true.
checks: Claude opens 10 rows (or 10 claims) at random and compares them with their source.

a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a guess written as a fact (say 'not found' instead)

tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: the function spec, written as the build plan
tasks.why: Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.
tasks.unlocks: Joseph goes pillar by pillar, function before form; this file is the plan Claude builds Kairos Meridian from, step by step.
steps: Open the live page (https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/kairos/) on a phone-sized browser and use every section.
Read the code (https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/pillars/kairos): every file the page loads, and pillar.json.
Write section A from what is there now, with file:line for each item; then B to H.
Write for Claude to build from: exact, testable, nothing vague like 'improve the UX'.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with exactly these headings, in this order: A What it does today | B What Joseph needs it to do | C Data | D Screens | E Rules and edge cases | F Acceptance tests | G Order of work | H Must not

fields.name: A What it does today
fields.rule: every section, control and number on the live page, each with the file and line in the code that makes it (e.g. app.js:142)

fields.name: B What Joseph needs it to do
fields.rule: 'As Joseph, when ..., I want ..., so that ...'; from the pillar's mission and its own data; never invent facts about his life

fields.name: C Data
fields.rule: record | field | type | unit | required | example | storage key (prometheus.<pillar>.<name>) | read by which other pillar

fields.name: D Screens
fields.rule: purpose; every element top to bottom; every number with its formula and source field; the empty state text; the error state

fields.name: E Rules and edge cases
fields.rule: dates and time zones, missing data, offline, two devices, a value of 0 vs unknown

fields.name: F Acceptance tests
fields.rule: Given / When / Then, each checkable in a phone browser in under two minutes

fields.name: G Order of work
fields.rule: each step small enough for one build, with what Joseph can use after it

fields.name: H Must not
fields.rule: the charter's protections that apply, no server or account, no made-up numbers

tasks.example: F7. Given an oil change logged at 12,000 mi and a 6,000 mi interval, when the odometer is set to 17,500 mi, then the service card shows 'due in 500 mi' in amber.
self_check: Every item in A has a file:line that exists.
B has 8+ stories and none invents a personal fact.
C names every field with type and example.
F has 12+ tests, each with one Given, one When, one Then.
G steps are in an order that can ship one by one.
